bookingWindow.title: One shipment before and after Direct’s booking cutoff
bookingWindow.sharedBasis: ORD-104; 100 units; Thursday noon–Friday 5 p.m. receiving window; $5,000 expense limit. Same quotes, resources, current confirmations and cost-first app.
bookingWindow.change: Assessment as of: 8 a.m. → 11:30 a.m. This one control updates current time and the earliest selection time together. All times are November 17, 2026, UTC−06:00.

panels.label: A · The cheaper option is still bookable

inputs.label: Carrier booking windows
inputs.value: Direct until 11 a.m.; Consolidated until noon

panels.explanation: Maya can meet the promise for less. She seeks the required authorization and reservation while Direct remains available.

figure.alt: The native SDK Decision summary prefers Direct at $4,000 while the $5,000 Consolidated arrangement also meets the recorded requirements.
figure.caption: At 8 a.m., Direct protects the delivery promise for less. The cost-first policy remains fixed.

panels.label: B · Direct’s booking window has closed

inputs.label: Carrier booking windows
inputs.value: The same 11 a.m. and noon cutoffs

panels.explanation: Maya can justify the $1,000 premium because Direct is no longer bookable for this unreserved shipment. Consolidated’s other requirements still pass.

figure.alt: At 11:30 a.m., Direct is past its 11 a.m. booking cutoff and Consolidated is preferred at $5,000.
figure.caption: The changed booking context justifies the $1,000 premium. The quotes and cost-first policy remain fixed.

bookingWindow.takeaway: One policy produces different supported proposals as the available responses change. Earlier arrival alone does not justify the premium; the closed booking window does.

confirmation.title: One revised order before and after a genuine current confirmation
confirmation.sharedBasis: ORD-105 revision 2; 100 units; 8 a.m.; $5,000 expense limit. Direct capacity stays 99, Backup stays $6,000, and the cost-first app and all other case inputs stay fixed.
confirmation.change: A newly received confirmation supplies SLOT-SHIP-105-REV2 for order revision 2 in place of the previous reference and revision-1 scope. The native before/after inputs retain every changed field.

panels.label: A · Confirmation covers the old order
panels.finding: Obtain current support · No arrangement passes
panels.explanation: Maya asks the carrier coordinator for a genuine current confirmation or escalates another response. A confirmed record for the old order is insufficient.

figure.alt: The revised order has no passing arrangement: Direct lacks capacity, Backup exceeds the spending boundary and Consolidated lacks current confirmation.
figure.caption: The compact comparison gives each arrangement its own condition to inspect.

panels.label: B · Newly received confirmation covers revision 2
panels.explanation: Maya reviews the newly received evidence and can put Consolidated forward. Direct still lacks capacity; Backup still exceeds the limit.

figure.alt: After applying a genuine revision-2 slot confirmation, the same shipment calculation prefers Consolidated at $5,000.
figure.caption: Direct remains capacity-blocked and Backup remains over the expense limit. The current confirmation changes Consolidated’s eligibility.

confirmation.takeaway: The justified response changes because the team obtained evidence that covers the actual order. Relabeling the old confirmation would manufacture support and is not the action demonstrated here.

authorConfirmation.title: The authored slot requirement with no confirmation and with a valid record
authorConfirmation.sharedBasis: One frozen arrival-first tutorial app; the same three quotes; 100 cases; $5,000 expense limit; $6,500 cash limit. Earliest eligible arrival is the unchanged priority.
authorConfirmation.change: The second case adds one confirmed slot record for the exact order, service and full loading window. The case identifier also differs; published rules, prices, permissions and timing parameters are identical.

panels.label: A · No current slot record
panels.explanation: Maya has a passing option. The new Consolidated quote cannot pass until the team has the required confirmation.

figure.alt: Frozen arrival-first tutorial decision without a slot confirmation: Direct is preferred, Consolidated fails the slot condition and Backup exceeds the budget.
figure.caption: Current production renderer of the frozen arrival-first tutorial. Without the scoped slot confirmation, Direct remains preferred.

navigationFigure.alt: The frozen arrival-first authoring app without a current slot record: Direct is preferred, Consolidated fails its slot requirement and Backup exceeds the expense limit.
navigationFigure.caption: The separate arrival-first tutorial without a slot confirmation. The current navigation preserves Direct as the preferred supported arrangement.

calculationFigure.alt: The frozen arrival-first authoring app without a current slot record prefers Direct, while Consolidated fails its slot requirement and Backup exceeds the limit.
calculationFigure.caption: Without a current slot confirmation, Direct remains preferred in the separate arrival-first tutorial.

panels.label: B · A valid scoped slot record
panels.explanation: Under this tutorial’s arrival-first priority, the confirmed service becomes preferred. The launch owner still justifies the premium and the responsible owner authorizes it.

figure.alt: The same frozen tutorial app with a valid slot record prefers Consolidated at $5,000; Direct still passes and Backup remains over budget.
figure.caption: Current production renderer of the frozen arrival-first tutorial. With the valid scoped record, Consolidated becomes preferred under the original arrival-first policy.

navigationFigure.alt: The same frozen arrival-first app with the valid scoped slot record: Consolidated is preferred at $5,000; Direct still passes and Backup remains over budget.
navigationFigure.caption: The same tutorial app with its valid scoped slot record. Consolidated becomes preferred under the unchanged arrival-first priority.

calculationFigure.alt: The same frozen arrival-first app with its valid scoped slot record prefers Consolidated at $5,000; Direct still passes and Backup remains over budget.
calculationFigure.caption: A valid scoped slot record makes Consolidated preferred under the unchanged arrival-first tutorial priority.

authorConfirmation.takeaway: The author defines what support the service needs. Colleagues then get different, explainable findings when that support is absent or present. This arrival-first tutorial is separate from the cost-first operating app.

batchCases.title: Two morning shipment contexts produce different interventions
batchCases.sharedBasis: The same cost-first shipment app and 8 a.m. assessment clock. Each independently allocated shipment needs 100 units by the original receiving deadline within a $5,000 expense limit.
batchCases.change: These are different shipments, not a single-field experiment: ORD-104 stays at revision 1 with complete support; ORD-105 is revision 2, Direct capacity is 99 and its Consolidated confirmation remains revision 1.

panels.label: A · ORD-104 retains complete support

inputs.label: Current scope
inputs.value: Order revision 1; current confirmation and permissions

panels.explanation: Maya checks the retained basis and passes the supported proposal to the responsible owner before Direct’s 11 a.m. carrier cutoff.

figure.alt: The actual CLI report for SHIP-104 shows Direct preferred at $4,000 and the complete alternatives.
figure.caption: The native morning report retains complete support for this shipment.

panels.label: B · ORD-105 has unresolved revision-2 support

inputs.label: Shipment and owner
inputs.value: SHIP-105 · Maya Chen; carrier coordinator obtains slot

inputs.label: Material exceptions
inputs.value: Direct: 99 of 100 units; Consolidated confirmation: revision 1

panels.finding: Obtain current confirmation or escalate · No arrangement passes
panels.explanation: The carrier coordinator must obtain actual support for revision 2. Maya cannot advance yesterday’s proposal as the current recommendation.

figure.alt: The actual CLI report for SHIP-105 separates capacity, spending and current-confirmation failures.
figure.caption: A different order context calls for obtaining the missing current support or escalating.

batchCases.takeaway: A batch review helps the owner distinguish work that can advance from work needing a specific intervention. The complete queue also separates old permissions and malformed source inputs.
